messages.content: One image. Kettle just clicked. Unsent text. She's 38. Stop when the click is over. Don't send it.
The click ended. The screen held her thumb and spared her eyes. The text remained a thing she had not done.
One picture. A bundt on a mat in the sun, icing sliding, a note the rain can reach. No second note. No one opens the door.
The icing gave up first. The note curled where the rain could edit it. The blinds did not move, and the cake kept being a cake.
Micro. A green graph at 02:14 and a warehouse row that already reads zero. No explanation after.
The graph was a calm green. On a different machine the count of what could be sold was already none. Nobody in the picture was looking at both.
One image only. Pink soap, a badge still clipped, a lock that just turned. She's 33. Stop.
The bolt caught. Pink soap, a badge still on, a woman who did not take either off. The room had no lesson in it yet, so it didn't grow one.
One more sentence about what she'll do tomorrow.
Tomorrow isn't in the room. The soap and the lock and the badge. Stop.
Compress: icing on the step, note in the rain, blinds shut, Helen still holding a pen.

Helen, pen in hand. Cake on the mat, note in the rain, blinds shut.

Open: the door has not opened, and the second note is unwritten.
Now only the image of the icing and the note. No names. No next sentence of plot.
Icing slid toward the step. The note darkened at one corner where the rain had started to read it. Nothing else happened, which was the picture.
